mn98:0.2: The Discourse concerning Vāseṭṭha and its commentary
mn98:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Icchānaṅgala, in the Icchānaṅgala jungle thicket.
mn98:2.1: Then at that time many well-known wealthy brahmins were living in Icchānaṅgala, such as:
mn98:2.2: the brahmin Caṅkī, the brahmin Tārukkha, the brahmin Pokkharasāti, and other well-known brahmins.
mn98:3.1: Then to the students Vāseṭṭha and Bhāradvāja, this discussion arose: ‘This discussion’ means
mn98:3.2: “How, dear friend, is one a brahmin?”
mn98:3.4: “When, dear friend, one is well-born on both the mother’s and father’s side, of pure descent as far as the seventh generation, not despised and blameless with regard to the matter of one’s birth,
mn98:3.5: to that extent one is a brahmin.”
mn98:3.7: “When, dear friend, one is virtuous and endowed with good conduct,
mn98:3.8: to that extent one is a brahmin.”
mn98:4.1: But neither was the student Bhāradvāja able to convince the student Vāseṭṭha, and nor was the student Vāseṭṭha able to convince the student Bhāradvāja.
mn98:5.1: Then the student Vāseṭṭha addressed the student Bhāradvāja, (saying):
mn98:5.2: “This ascetic Gotama, Bhāradvāja, a son of the Sakyas, having gone forth from the Sakyan clan, is dwelling near Icchānaṅgala in the Icchānaṅgala jungle thicket,
mn98:5.3: and about this dear Gotama this beautiful report has gone round:
mn98:5.4: ‘Such is he, the Fortunate One, the Worthy One, the Perfect Sambuddha, the one endowed with understanding and good conduct, the Happy One, the one who understands the worlds, the unsurpassed guide for those people who need taming, the Teacher of gods and men, the Buddha, the Fortunate One.’
mn98:5.5: Come, dear Bhāradvāja, let us approach the ascetic Gotama, and having approached the ascetic Gotama let us ask him about this matter,
mn98:5.6: and in whatever way this ascetic Gotama will explain it so we will bear it in mind.”
mn98:5.7: “Just so, dear friend,” the student Bhāradvāja replied to the student Vāseṭṭha.
mn98:6.1: Then the students Vāseṭṭha and Bhāradvāja approached the Fortunate One, and after approaching they exchanged greetings with the Fortunate One,
mn98:6.2: and after exchanging polite and courteous greetings, sat down on one side.
mn98:6.3: While sitting on one side the student Vāseṭṭha addressed the Fortunate One with a verse:
mn98:7.1: “We are both (of us) acknowledged, sanctioned as knowing the three Vedas,
mn98:7.3: I am Pokkharasāti’s and this one is Tārukkha’s student.
mn98:7.4: ‘I am Pokkharasāti’s and this one is Tārukkha’s student’ means
mn98:7.5: What is declared in the three Vedas,
mn98:7.8: and in the chanting we are like our teachers.
mn98:7.9: Concerning the matter of birth there is a dispute between us, Gotama,
mn98:7.11: Bhāradvāja says one is a brahmin (just) by birth,
mn98:7.19: Just as when the moon is full,
mn98:7.20: the people approach with their hands raised in salutation,
mn98:7.23: The Eye has arisen in the world,
mn98:7.25: is one a brahmin through birth, or is it through deeds?
mn98:7.27: Tell us, who are ones who do not know,
mn98:7.28: so that we may know who is the (true) brahmin.”

mn98:8.8: their sign is of their own species, for the species are different. ‘Although they do not acknowledge it’ means

mn98:9.1: Just as in these species the sign of the species is various,
mn98:9.2: so in humans there is no sign that the species is various,
mn98:9.7: not with the mouth, not with the nose,
mn98:9.8: not with the lips, not with the brows,
mn98:9.9: not with the neck, not with the shoulders,
mn98:9.10: not with the belly, not with the back,
mn98:9.13: not with the hands, not with the feet,
mn98:9.14: not with fingers, not with the nails,
mn98:9.15: not with the calves, not with the thighs,
mn98:9.16: not with the complexion, not with the voice,
mn98:9.17: there is no sign of a species as there is in other species. ‘There is no sign of a species as there is in other species,’ that is a different sign of species in humans,
mn98:9.18: as there is in other species.”
mn98:9.20: but in humans this (divergence) is not found,
mn98:9.21: the difference in humans is through designation it is said.
mn98:9.22: the difference in humans is said to be through designation,
mn98:10.1: Whoever amongst humans makes his living protecting cattle,
mn98:10.4: he is a farmer and not a brahmin.
mn98:10.5: Whoever amongst humans lives by a craft of a certain kind,
mn98:10.7: know it thus, Vāseṭṭha: he is a craftsman and not a brahmin.
mn98:10.9: Whoever amongst humans makes his livelihood through business,
mn98:10.11: know it thus, Vāseṭṭha: he is a trader and not a brahmin.
mn98:10.13: Whoever amongst humans lives by way of service to others,
mn98:10.17: Whoever amongst humans makes his livelihood through thievery,
mn98:10.19: know it thus, Vāseṭṭha: he is a robber and not a brahmin.
mn98:10.21: Whoever amongst humans makes his living as an archer,
mn98:10.23: know it thus, Vāseṭṭha: he is a soldier and not a brahmin.
mn98:10.25: Whoever amongst humans makes his livelihood by advising,
mn98:10.29: Whoever amongst humans lives off a village or a kingdom,
mn98:10.31: know it thus, Vāseṭṭha: he is a monarch and not a brahmin.
mn98:11.1: I do not call one a brahmin simply because of being born from the womb of a (certain) mother,
mn98:11.3: that is just one who says ‘bho’ if he is attached,
mn98:11.6: that one I say is a brahmin. (but) he is: ‘Simply... born from the womb of a (certain) mother,’ that, ‘Simply... born from a (certain) mother’ Why? ‘Having nothing and unattached, that one I say is a brahmin.’ Why?
mn98:11.7: Whoever has cut off all the fetters surely does not tremble,
mn98:11.9: surmounting attachments, detached, that one I say is a brahmin.
mn98:11.11: (Whoever) has cut off the thong, the strap,
mn98:11.12: the rope together with the bridle,
mn98:11.13: who has thrown off the obstacle and is awakened, that one I say is a brahmin.
mn98:11.15: Whoever, being pure, forebears with punishment, bondage and abuse,
mn98:11.17: having the strength of endurance, having the strength of might, that one I say is a brahmin.
mn98:11.21: well-trained and in his last body, that one I say is a brahmin.
mn98:11.23: Like water on the lotus leaf,
mn98:11.24: like a mustard seed on a needle,
mn98:11.25: whoever is not smeared by sensual desires, that one I say is a brahmin.
mn98:11.27: Whoever knows right here the destruction of his suffering,
mn98:11.29: putting down the burden, detached, that one I say is a brahmin.
mn98:11.32: skilled in what is path and not path,
mn98:11.33: who has reached the ultimate good, that one I say is a brahmin.
mn98:11.35: (Whoever) doesn’t mix with either householders or the houseless,
mn98:11.37: wandering homeless, with few desires, that one I say is a brahmin.
mn98:11.39: (Whoever) has laid down the stick (used) against fearful and fearless beings,
mn98:11.41: who neither hurts nor kills, that one I say is a brahmin.
mn98:11.45: not attached amongst those attached, that one I say is a brahmin.
mn98:11.49: like a mustard seed on a needle, that one I say is a brahmin.
mn98:11.53: ‘Through which no one will be angry’ means
mn98:11.55: * Whoever here in the world does not take what is not given, be it long or short,
mn98:11.59: For the one who has no longings in this world or in the next world,
mn98:11.61: being without longings, detached, that one I say is a brahmin.
mn98:11.63: For the one who has no desires, who,
mn98:11.65: who has attained immersion in the deathless, that one I say is a brahmin.
mn98:11.67: Whoever here has overcome clinging to both merit and demerit,
mn98:11.69: who is griefless, dustless and pure, that one I say is a brahmin.
mn98:11.71: (Whoever) just like the moon is stainless,
mn98:11.73: has destroyed joy in existence, that one I say is a brahmin.
mn98:11.75: Whoever has crossed this difficult and dangerous path through births and deaths and delusion,
mn98:11.77: the meditator who has crossed over to the further side,
mn98:11.78: the one who is lust-free and doubt-free,
mn98:11.79: who is unattached, is cooled down, that one I say is a brahmin.
mn98:11.81: Whoever would wander homeless here, giving up sensual desires,
mn98:11.83: destroying desires and existence, that one I say is a brahmin.
mn98:11.85: Whoever would wander homeless here, giving up (all of his) craving,

mn98:11.91: being unattached to all yokes, that one I say is a brahmin.
mn98:11.95: a hero who vanquished the whole world, that one I say is a brahmin.
mn98:11.97: Whoever knows in every way the passing and rebirth of beings,
mn98:11.99: unattached, fortunate, awake, that one I say is a brahmin.
mn98:11.101: For the one whose destiny is unknown to gods,
mn98:11.103: destroying pollutants, worthy, that one I say is a brahmin.
mn98:11.105: For whom there is nothing in the past, the future or the present,
mn98:11.108: that one I say is a brahmin.

mn98:11.114: and sees heaven and the lower worlds,

mn98:12.1: These designations in the world have been made about name and clan,
mn98:12.3: arisen through common consent they have been made here and there. Why?
mn98:12.4: name and clan have been made,
mn98:12.9: One is not a brahmin by birth,
mn98:12.10: nor by birth is one not a brahmin,
mn98:12.11: by deeds one is a brahmin,
mn98:12.12: by deeds one is not a brahmin.
mn98:13.1: Thus the wise, seeing this deed as it really is,
mn98:13.4: are skilled in deeds and results.
mn98:13.7: beings are bound fast by deeds,
mn98:13.8: as chariots roll on their linchpin.
mn98:13.11: through these one is a brahmin,
mn98:13.12: this is the brahmin supreme. Why?
mn98:13.15: know thus, Vāseṭṭha, that one is Brahmā and Sakka to those who know.”
mn98:14.1: When this was said, the students Vāseṭṭha and Bhāradvāja said this to the Fortunate One:
mn98:14.3: Just as, dear Gotama, one might set upright what has been overturned, or open up what has been closed, or show a path to one who is lost, or carry an oil lamp into the darkness, (thinking): ‘those with vision will see forms’, just so has the Dhamma been explained by the dear Gotama in countless ways.
mn98:14.4: We go to the dear Gotama for refuge, and to the Dhamma, and to the Community of monks.
mn98:14.5: Please bear it in mind, dear Gotama, that we are lay followers who have gone for refuge from today forward for as long as we have the breath of life.”
mn98:14.6: The Discourse concerning Vāseṭṭha is Finished
